text:
Anna: Heads up — seeing a perf regression after kernel v3.4.1 rollout (~22:09 UTC). p99 token latency +35% on /generate for seq_len>1024. Alert burn-rate fired for ~12m.

Deploy-bot: deploy finished 2026-02-10T22:09:48Z by @Mike (kernel v3.4.1) :white_check_mark:

Mike: Repro'd locally with the load generator. Quick flamegraph uploaded: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/profiles/flame-1789001234.svg

Mike: perf top snippet (sampling):
```
  samples   %   symbol
  12000   32.1  kernel_attention::compute
  5200    13.9  kv_cache::lookup
  4000    10.7  batching::dispatch
```

Sarah: Grafana numbers from the 22:00–22:30 window: p95 /generate went 45ms -> 70ms, p99 120ms -> 165ms for long sequences. Query I used (PromQL):
```
sum by (route,le) (rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]))
```

Lee: My first guess: kernel selection heuristic flipped to prefer the small-batch optimized path (`--prefer-small-batch=true`) and for long seqs we hit an inefficient fallback that copies KV state. That explains both improved small-batch throughput and worse tail for long sequences.

Jordan: Can we toggle `prefer_small_batch=false` on the canary? Quick A/B test to see effect on p99. If throughput suffers we can route only seq_len>1024 to legacy kernel.

Anna: Ops, please page if burn-rate stays >1.5x for >10m on user-facing routes. We already hit 1.6x for ~12m.

Ops-bot: Pager opened — incident INC-2026-034. Burn-rate exceeded threshold for route=/generate between 22:12–22:24 UTC. Paging on-call: @Lee

Lee: Oncall here. I'm adding a short-term routing rule to send seq_len>1024 traffic to model-variant v2 (legacy kernel) and throttling background batch jobs. Applying now.

Mike: Microbench results: legacy kernel p99 ~115ms, new kernel p99 ~165ms (seq>1024). Small-batch throughput up ~9% on new kernel. Suggest we split routing by seq_len for now.

Anna: Agreed. We need a dashboard panel showing token-level p50/p95/p99, kernel_variant ratio, and per-route burn-rate. Panel should break down by seq_len buckets (<=256, 257–1024, >1024).

Sarah: Draft panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/token-latency?orgId=1&panelId=42
Query example: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,route,kernel_variant))`

Jordan: I'll also tune the anomaly detector: lower false positives from background replication traffic and focus sensitivity on routes tagged `user-facing`. Opening PR to alerts repo now.

Anna: For the immediate mitigation keep the diversion in place. If the canary config toggle doesn't improve tail by EOD, rollback the kernel change. Also add a unit/integration test that simulates mixed seq_len traffic to catch selection regressions.

Mike: Will attach pprof and a short runbook once the next validation run completes. Quick pprof snapshot suggests heavy time in attention kernel memcpy paths — attaching profile after upload.

Ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated — routing diversion applied at 22:34 UTC. Monitoring period: 30m.

Anna: Thanks. Follow-up actions: (1) add dashboard panel and alert rule refinement, (2) unit test for kernel selection heuristics, (3) postmortem in #postmortems when stabilized.

Mike: I'll drop the pprof link and the minimal repro steps into the incident thread after validation.

Lee: Oncall note: if anyone wants to experiment, use the canary flag `kernel_variant=legacy` for seq_len>1024. Keep changes small.

Jordan: PR to alerts repo: https://github.com/redwood/alerts/pull/427 — reduces sensitivity for non-user routes, adds an alternate burn-rate window for token-level alerts.

Anna: Great. Closing the immediate thread — will reconvene after verification.
